Accused in Special Case (POCSO) No.7/2024 pending before the Court of Additional District and Sessions Judge/Special Judge at Bidar arising out of Crime No.60/2023 registered by Bidar Women police station, Bidar, for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 376, 366 and 376(2)(n) of IPC and under Sections 4, 6, 8 and 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for short 'POCSO Act') is before this Court under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. seeking regular bail.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties.

sentences.text:
3. The FIR in Crime No.60/2023 was registered by Bidar Women police station, Bidar against the petitioner herein initially for the offence punishable under Section NC: 2024:KHC-K:3874 363 of IPC on the basis of the first information dated 05.10.2023 received from respondent No.2 herein,
who is the father of the victim girl.
During the course of investigation, the petitioner and victim girl were traced together in Bihar State and they were brought back.
The petitioner was produced before the Court and remanded to judicial custody on 08.11.2023.
The victim girl was medically examined and her statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. was recorded by the jurisdictional Magistrate on 15.11.2023.
The investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed against the petitioner for the aforesaid offences.
The bail application filed by the petitioner before the jurisdictional Sessions Court in Crl.Misc.No.172/2024 was rejected on 25.04.2024.
Therefore, the petitioner is before this Court.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioner having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition submits that the victim girl has not made any allegations against the petitioner in her statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:3874 and she has also turned hostile before the Trial Court.
He submits that the victim girl had voluntarily accompanied the petitioner.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for respondent No.1 has opposed the bail petition.
He submits that the victim girl is a minor and therefore, alleged offences would got attracted against the petitioner.
6. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that he has no objection for granting bail to the petitioner.

7. The material on record would go to show that after the victim girl was found missing from her house on 04.10.2023, respondent No.2 herein, who is her father had approached the police on 05.10.2023 and submitted his first information, based on which, FIR in Crime No.60/2023 was registered against the petitioner.
During the course of investigation, the petitioner and the victim girl were traced together in the village of the petitioner in NC: 2024:KHC-K:3874 Bihar State and they were brought back.
The victim girl was produced before the jurisdictional Magistrate and her statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. was recorded on 15.11.2023.
She has not stated anything as against the petitioner and on the other hand she has only stated that she intends to marry the petitioner.
During the course of trial, the victim girl is examined before the Trial Court as PW.1 and the first informant is examined as PW.2.

PW.1 and PW.2 have not supported the case of the prosecution and therefore, they have been treated as hostile witnesses before the Trial Court and though they are cross-examined by the Public Prosecutor, nothing has been elicited from their mouth.
The petitioner, who is aged about 20 years, is in custody from 08.11.2023.
Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that the petitioner has made out a prima facie case for grant of bail.
Accordingly, following order is passed:
ORDER The petition is allowed.
